deviceEditor.bridgeNotConnected: The bridge is not connected right now. Check that it is running.
deviceEditor.allowMac: If your Mac asks whether the bridge may find devices on your local network, click Allow there. The search carries on by itself.
deviceEditor.allowOther: If the bridge’s computer asks whether the bridge may find devices on your network, allow it there. The search carries on by itself.
deviceEditor.looking: Looking for printers on your network…
deviceEditor.stillLooking: Still looking on your other networks.
deviceEditor.noneFound: No printer found. Check that the printer is switched on and on the same network as the bridge's computer, then search again, or add it by its address below.
deviceEditor.notFoundSummary: Printer not found? Add it by its address
deviceEditor.addressPlaceholder: for example 192.168.1.50, or 192.168.1.50:7130 for another port
deviceEditor.keyOrPasswordHint: (only if the printer asks for one: a Klipper printer's Moonraker API key, a Prusa printer's PrusaLink password, an OctoPrint API key, a Bambu Lab printer's LAN access code; an Elegoo needs none)
deviceEditor.keysToBridge: API keys go to the bridge, which keeps them on its computer; Cloud Slicer doesn't store them.
deviceEditor.clickAdd: Click Add on each printer you want. When they're ready, the button at the bottom adds them all.
deviceEditor.name: Name
deviceEditor.goesToBridge: It goes to the bridge, not to Cloud Slicer.
deviceEditor.connectingBridgeHelp: This takes a few seconds, longer if the bridge has only just started.
deviceEditor.joinedHelp: It's in your account and starts with that computer.
deviceEditor.stillTrying: Still trying: this changes by itself as soon as the bridge answers.
deviceEditor.removesPrinter: This removes {{name}} from Cloud Slicer. The printer itself isn't changed.
deviceEditor.removesBridgePrinter: This removes {{name}} from Cloud Slicer and from its bridge. The printer itself isn't changed.
deviceEditor.bridgeStays: The bridge stays. To remove the bridge too, use Printers & bridges.
deviceEditor.throughExisting: Add it through a bridge you already have
deviceEditor.orNewOnOther: Or set up a new bridge on another computer:
deviceEditor.orNew: Or set up a new bridge
deviceEditor.notPairingLink: That isn't a pairing link. Copy the whole address of the page the bridge opened.
deviceEditor.updateToFind: To find and add printers from here, update the bridge: download it again and open it (or run the Terminal command again).
deviceEditor.directIntro: For a printer you've put on the internet yourself, behind https.
deviceEditor.corsSteps: First, let this site talk to the printer. Moonraker only answers websites it lists in cors_domains. On the printer, open moonraker.conf (in Mainsail or Fluidd: Machine, then moonraker.conf), add this site under [authorization], save, and restart Moonraker:
deviceEditor.corsHasSection: If <c>[authorization]</c> already has <c>cors_domains:</c>, add just the last line under it, indented like the others.
deviceEditor.tailscale: Using Tailscale (built into the paxx12 U1 firmware)? Turn on Tailscale Serve on the printer and enter its https://….ts.net address. It works from your phones and computers that are signed in to Tailscale.
